assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational account of collateral constraints and amplification that reshaped macroeconomic analysis of credit cycles and policy.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore supply the central collateral mechanism; Gertler is a principal architect of its monetary-macro integration.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been extensively developed, used in policy analysis, and tested against repeated financial disruptions.
uncertainties: The appropriate division of credit among the listed contributors is broader than a three-person award can fully represent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work made political incentives, institutions, and state capacity central to rigorous analysis of fiscal policy and development.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini established much of the modern comparative political-economy framework, while Besley made defining contributions on accountability and state capacity.
assessment.maturity: The research program is longstanding and has generated a durable theoretical and empirical literature.
uncertainties: The umbrella is broad, making the precise discovery framing important.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantifying misallocation provided a powerful common language for explaining large productivity and income differences across countries.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow supplied the especially influential empirical-accounting formulation, with Restuccia a central contributor to the broader quantitative program.
assessment.maturity: The mechanism has been widely applied and debated across countries, industries, and policy settings.
uncertainties: Measured wedges need not map cleanly to particular distortions or policy remedies.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models materially changed how macroeconomists analyze distribution, consumption responses, and policy transmission.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll, and Violante are tightly associated with the influential formulation and its macroeconomic implications.
assessment.maturity: The approach is now a major component of modern macroeconomic research and policy discussion.
uncertainties: Its relatively recent development leaves less time than older frameworks for cumulative confirmation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative-data research transformed measurement of intergenerational mobility and connected local conditions to life chances.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are central to the mobility program, with Friedman a major contributor to its data and policy applications.
assessment.maturity: The work has yielded a large body of follow-on research and unusually direct policy relevance.
uncertainties: The causal interpretation of geographic and institutional correlations remains difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their analysis extended dynamic economic reasoning to exhaustible resources, natural capital, biodiversity, and sustainability.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are closely linked to foundational work on resource constraints and intergenerational welfare.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is long-established and increasingly consequential as environmental constraints enter economic policy analysis.
uncertainties: The broad environmental-economics framing overlaps with several adjacent intellectual traditions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework gave monetary policy a coherent microfounded account of nominal rigidities and stabilization.
assessment.attribution: Woodford and Gali were central to the modern policy framework, while Calvo's pricing specification became a core workhorse device.
assessment.maturity: This is a deeply mature framework with major influence on central-bank analysis and macroeconomic teaching.
uncertainties: The candidate grouping contains many indispensable contributors, so any limited laureate selection is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their long-run comparative evidence made financial-crisis and sovereign-debt histories far more central to macroeconomic analysis.
assessment.attribution: Reinhart and Rogoff are jointly identified with the principal cross-country historical data and synthesis.
assessment.maturity: The work has had sustained academic and policy influence over many years.
uncertainties: Some prominent empirical claims and interpretations have been challenged, requiring careful separation of the data contribution from stronger causal conclusions.
